questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to South of Italy. Here in Trento,

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was nice because I made friends and travelled and Saw a lot of places. The Erasmus Grant made a lot of things possible.

However, it has been a bit stressfull with the whole OLA-show and administrative deadlines. It was not always possible to get the help you needed in time (I felt like at least)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit difficult, because of Long answer times to my Home university and I could have needed more detailed instructions, helping you through all the different steps, that has felt a bit like a puzzle.

However, the staff in Trento are super nice and helpfull, and is super willing to help you. You just have to reach out

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have a physical Office with Office hours where you can drop by and get help + a telephone number you Can call. I would highly recommend this to my Home university as you Can call or show up and get help. Which definetly helps with Solving out things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

My recommendation is to book a room as soon as you’ve been sprogede for Exchange. Then  good places are available

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everyone does in Trento

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There’s a bit of a houses crisis in Trento, as in many other cities. Some people didn’t find a place to stay, but mostly those who we’re in last minute.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing/different, and i struggled to know whether to contact my Home or host university and the whole OLA process was a confusing (for me at least). But I managed and you Will manage as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My contact person in Trento was very helpfull through it all and answered quickly. But back at KU, I struggled a bit to know who to contact, and they had a 10-day answering Max, which I thought was a lot in these strict deadline times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do things in good times before the deadline. And ask.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took an italian language course, 3 BA courses and 1 MA course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mostly just lectures you show up to and a written 2 hours exam in the end. At Home we mostly write longer papers as exam

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
A1, italian
Introduction to italian culture
Major issues in international politics
The european union and its neighbours
Social inequelities and education

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to italian culture, because you learn interesteeing things about italian culture and you get variation from normal courses.

Italian A1 (intensive course) ud you wanna learn italian and get 3 ECTS for this. Its a bit intense though, as its in 2,5 weeks

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Travel insurance etc.
Travel costs to different cities in Italy!
Food/drinks when going out

You usually use a bit more money in food/drinks, because you’re initialt and on Erasmus. I’d largely say that the prices for food is the same in the supermarkets in Trento, as for Denmark. However, Wine is generalkonsul much cheaper, bortvis supermarkets and out at bars.

In terms of public transport, we blitz the circulation pass for 70€, enabling a 1 year subscription on “free” transport in the whole Trentino region. This has been very usefull and worth it for us. It can for example be used for taking a direct bus til Lake Garda (1,5 hours)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Wine is cheaper. And eating out is a bit cheaper Maybe.

Its difficult to give an estimate of what everything costs (above) because it varies a lot from every week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Very Satisfied. 

There is a free gym (small though, but it works), called Palestra rossa.

There are a lot of beautyful makes, that are soo nice to visit in summer, and many pretty mountains to use for hiking, skiing or climbing. Many sporty people in Trento.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are different sports available, but most people do hiking, climbing or skiing at least. They have some special offers for us though, on their website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go visit lakes; Lake garda and Lago di lamar are my favourites.

Go on a lot of hikes during summer.

Climb outside at the cliffs.

Participate in a lot of ESN (Erasmus student network) events, and their trips (for example, I went with Them to october fest in munic)

Visit a lot of cities in Italy with other Erasmus students, and make friends. I visited Florence, Rome, Venice, Bologna, Milan and verona, which are all nearby.

Use the ESN discounts on Ryanair, Spotahome (apartment rents for travels during the semester) and FlixBus. You can use theese from when you get your ESN card after arrival.

Visit countries around Italy, Austria, Slovenia, Hungary…

Go on ski trips. You can also buy a whole-season dolomites ski pass for 900€ ish.

Go to Decathlon and buy/rent sport equipment.

Go to Scarletta (the bar everyone goes to) and go to kareoke on baccus on tuesdays.

Use the big Erasmus Whatsapp group to arrange events for everyone

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: What I wrote above!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not bad.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and talk to people in class, on bars or when meeting Them in the bus or whatever.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
They don’t have the same relationship to, that its respectfull to be silent in public spaces, eg the bus. They just listen to loud things in their phones, without headphones.

Many local people don’t speak english. Some people won’t even try to inkluder you with the english they can, for different reasons.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
People are very chill, and mostly happy. 

The food culture is good

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Trento is a relatively small city. However, it offers a lot as it is in the dolamites, close to mountains and lakes etc. go here, if you want to take advantage of all these opportunities around the city.

The small city means, that the nightlife is for example not the biggest. However, we’re 300 Erasmus students in a small city, and we meet each others on the street and at the bar evwryone goes to. This is super cozy. Consider if this would suit you.

Be open, prioritize experiences and adventures over School, and have fun. Enjoy your Erasmus!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Buy the circulation pass and use it to explore the whole trentino region

Use the free gym, Palestra rossa, using the app “opera4you”

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting friends from norway and sweden and travelling italy with Them.
And having a friend group where we chill and have fun every day, knowing that we of course also will hang out tomorrow.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The administrative things.

And also, my apartment was not the cleaned maybe. But you know, you manage and you get use to it. So don’t stay Home just because of that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
